newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's ASC begins action against Nomura.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's ASC begins action against Nomura.

text.p: The Australian Securities Commission (ASC) said on Tuesday it had begun Federal Court proceedings against Nomura International Plc following a year-long investigation into share-market dealings.

It said the action was the result of an ASC investigation in share trading on the Australian Stock Exchange in March 1996 and the share price index (SPI) futures contract on the Sydney Futures Exchange on March 29 last year.

"We were unable to agree with Nomura as to the nature of these events and we have today instituted proceedings in Sydney in the Federal Court against Nomura International alleging market manipulation and seeking remedies against the company," New South Wales regional comissioner Bill Coad told reporters.

In a statement, the ASC alleges that the conduct engaged in by Nomura in connection with the sale of securities amounted to market manipulation, wash trading, misleading and deceptive conduct in connection with securities dealings and conduct calculated to create a false or misleading appearance with respect to the price of the SPI contract.
The ASC said it was seeking injunctions against Nomura to prevent conduct of this nature happening again.
While Nomura had co-operated, the ASC said it understood Nomura denied the allegations and had indicated it would contest the allegations with mediation attempts having failed.
"Nomura have been very co-operative in these inquiries in London, in Hong Kong and here, but there is a point of serious disagreement," Coad said.
Proceedings brought were civil in nature with no criminal prosecutions against individuals or the company.
"There is no criminal proceedings at all in prospect nor would they be feasible in these circumstances," ASC national director of enforcement Joe Longo told reporters.
